newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Santos buys three sugar mills from Emvasa.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Santos buys three sugar mills from Emvasa.

text.p: Mexican sugar mill owners Ingenios Santos bought three more mills from shareholders of the Impulsora Marcas Mexicanas, the bottlers Embotelladores del Valle de Anahuac (Emvasa) said Wednesday.

Emvasa, a major shareholder of Impulsora Marcas Mexicanas, said it would receive around $13 million for its shareholding in the sale, part in cash and part in sugar, with a maximum payment period of 24 months.
Emvasa did not say what its share holding was in Impulsora Marcas Mexicanas, nor what was the total sale value of the three mills.
"At the same time of the sale of the shares held by Emvasa, other share holders have agreed to sell their stakes to Ingenios Santos," Emvasa said in a statement to the Mexican Stock Exchange.
Impulsora Marcas Mexicanas comprises three sugar mills, namely Plan de Ayala, San Gabriel and Cuatotolapan, whose official name is Compania Industrial Azucarera.

Ingenios Santos is owned by the family of Mexican senator and businessman Alberto Santos, also owners of Monterrey-based cookie makers Gamesa. Ingenios Santos will already has the Pedernales, Alianza Popular and Bellavista sugar mills.
Aside the sale, Emvasa and Ingenios Santos agreed on a strategic alliance in which the bottler has promised to acquire 40,000 tonnes of sugar per annum over the next five years.
((--Chris Aspin, Mexico City newsroom (525) 7289530. E-mail at chris.aspin@reuters.com))
